record.context_brief: Rational solutions for smallest open examples
record.original_question: Find explicit parametrizations or another complete description of all rational solutions to the Diophantine equations y^2 + z^2 = x^3 + 1, y^2 + z^2 = x^3 - 1, and y^2 - x^2 y + z^2 + 1 = 0.

evidence.quote: If we ask the same question about rational solutions, then the smallest open are the same equations (3) and (4), as well as the equation y^2 - x^2y + z^2 + 1 = 0 (5).
We know that the corresponding cubic surfaces are unirational, see https://mathoverflow.net/questions/452461/, but currently do not know explicit parametrizations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Provide either an explicit rational parametrization (i.e. a finite collection of rational maps from affine spaces to the variety whose images jointly cover all rational points, possibly outside a lower-dimensional exceptional set) or another complete description of the set of all rational solutions $(x,y,z) \in \mathbb{Q}^3$ to each of the following Diophantine equations:

(a) $y^2 + z^2 = x^3 + 1$,

(b) $y^2 + z^2 = x^3 - 1$,

(c) $y^2 - x^2 y + z^2 + 1 = 0$.

It is known that the corresponding affine cubic surfaces are unirational over $\mathbb{Q}$; the task is to give an explicit complete description (e.g. an explicit unirational/rational parametrization) of the rational points on each of these three surfaces.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up explicit rational parametrizations for the surfaces $y^2+z^2=x^3\pm 1$ or $y^2-x^2y+z^2+1=0$. While smooth cubic surfaces over algebraically closed fields are known to be rational (Clebsch 1866), and these particular surfaces are known to be unirational over $\mathbb{Q}$, no explicit parametrization or complete description of their rational points appears to be available in the literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Cubic surface - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Smooth cubic surfaces over algebraically closed fields are rational (Clebsch 1866); over Q the situation is more subtle and explicit parametrizations are not always known.
status_evidence.claim: General theory establishes rationality over algebraically closed fields but explicit Q-parametrizations of specific cubic surfaces such as the ones in question are not provided.

status_evidence.title: On the Parametrization over Q of Cubic Surfaces - René Pannekoek
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the difficulty of giving explicit parametrizations of cubic surfaces over Q.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit Q-parametrizations of cubic surfaces are nontrivial and not generally known case-by-case.
